correctness.rationale: The generator of a current-coordinate cylinder observable is \(h(X_0)[-\gamma X_0+\beta f(X_{-\tau})]\), so invariance for arbitrary continuous h gives \(\mathbb E[\beta f(X_{-\tau})\mid X_0]=\gamma X_0\). Semiflow invariance under one delay implies equal marginals for the delayed and current evaluations. Conditional orthogonality then gives the exact variance defect. Zero defect makes the current derivative vanish almost surely; invariance propagates this to all future times, and after one delay every history segment is constant, so the invariant measure is equilibrium-supported. For non-equilibrium measures, the strict defect plus the Lipschitz variance inequality yields \(\beta L_{m,M}>\gamma\). The packaged checker verifies the moment algebra and the three classical slope roots.

value.rationale: The defining feature of Mackey–Glass dynamics is that present decay is balanced against nonlinear production evaluated one full delay in the past. The accepted theorem identifies that delayed production as an exact regression target of the present concentration under every compact stationary state, turning the delay mechanism into a measurable stationary constraint rather than merely a trajectory equation. The associated variance identity quantifies exactly how much nonlinear-production fluctuation remains after conditioning on the current state, and its equality class separates equilibria from genuinely time-dependent recurrence. The support-dependent slope obstruction further converts the identity into an amplitude restriction: any recurrent stationary range must reach a region where delayed-feedback sensitivity is strong enough to beat instantaneous decay. This is useful for periodic and chaotic invariant data and is not a recomputation of a known Hopf or period-doubling threshold.
